platform: Windows; system Windows PowerShell 5.1; .NET Framework csc builds isolated synthetic installers

commands.detail: Rechecked the final launcher with a cache path containing spaces, ampersand, Chinese characters and apostrophe.

verified: Stable semantic version comparison: 0.7.10 > 0.7.9; drafts, prereleases, duplicates and wrong architecture rejected.
Only official Wbox GitHub asset URLs accepted; HTTPS and exact CDN host redirect allowlist.
SHA256SUMS and optional GitHub asset digest agree; size and SHA256 are streamed before installation.
Checking metadata never downloads an EXE; explicit acceptance starts one main-process job.
Progress and speed continue without renderer subscribers; speed drops to zero when bytes stop, sampler stops on completion.
Ready download can be retried after handoff failure; interrupted downloads become retryable after restart.
Installer helper waits for Wbox and backend exit and rechecks SHA256 before starting the package.
Synthetic installer success (0), user cancellation (2/5), failure (3), wrapped Windows elevation-required (740) then UAC refusal (1223).
Package exists while the installer runs, is removed only after confirmed exit, and app restart preserves the reconnect decision.
The actual helper survives termination of the Node process which launched it; no detached console lifetime assumption.
Locked package is retained for next startup cleanup; completed record ignores stale PID, orphan record compares PID, creation time and exact executable path.
Updater directory initialization failure disables update controls with a visible message and allows normal app startup.
Persisted path traversal cannot delete files outside updater-owned validated filenames.

cleanup.testFixtures: Each test creates a uniquely named temporary directory, verifies its absolute prefix before recursive removal, waits for child processes, and removes synthetic EXEs/sources/metadata.
cleanup.production: Update package and partial file cleanup is constrained to validated Wbox filenames. Helper code runs from the bundled string, creating no script file. Session/lock/result metadata is removed by the restarted app after helper release. Occupied files retain the session for retry at a later startup.

limits: UAC refusal is simulated using a test-only PowerShell cmdlet double throwing wrapped Win32 errors; no production validation bypass exists.
The actual installer was compiled but not installed over the user environment. Packaged UI, renderer release/reopen and archive dependency checks passed; see the linked reports.
